policy: Only sources with currently usable public inspiration material are active. An account may be used only when the user is authorized to use it; access controls, paywalls, security interstitials, and private content are never bypassed. Sources marked inactive remain as an audit trail and cannot be selected for a project dossier. Each active source declares how its entries can actually be retrieved: 'fetch' means a plain HTTP request exposes entry links and images, 'browser' means entries render only in a real browser session, so a plain fetch that returns a script shell or a rate-limit response is not evidence that the source is unavailable. Source admission is quality first: selected references come only from award or curated sources, while a submission feed may be browsed but cannot supply a selected reference. Individual selection is then brief fit, never random choice or tag convenience. Visit and record each candidate and establish its fit to the website's audience, business model, customer tasks, content topology, required routes and states, material, constraints, and time or cultural register. Reject an eligible site when its structure, behavior, content demands, or production reality do not transfer to this brief. Curation is an eligibility floor, not proof that an individual site is useful. Filtering a bulk feed by register produces register-matched mediocrity.
